**Archived at Zenodo:** [doi:10.5281/zenodo.24168406](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24168406). This DOI always resolves to the latest release of the maintained version.

```{r setup}
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

here::i_am("README.qmd")

output <- \(file) here::here("maintained", "output", file)
gt <- read_csv(here::here("ground_truth", "murphy_etal_2026_ground_truth.csv"),
               col_types = cols(.default = col_character(), value_rewrite = col_double(),
                                match_rewrite = col_double(), holds = col_double()))
floats <- read_csv(here::here("ground_truth", "float_coverage.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
controls <- read_csv(here::here("ground_truth", "negative_controls.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
spine <- read_csv(here::here("errata_entries.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
comparison <- read_csv(output("archive_output_comparison.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
verdicts <- read_csv(output("archive_script_verdicts.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
slopes <- read_csv(output("corrected_slopes.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
manifest <- read_csv(here::here("original_manifest.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
members <- read_csv(here::here("original_members_manifest.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
run_log <- read_lines(output("archive_run.log"))
claim_summary_line <- str_subset(run_log, "^CLAIM SUMMARY") |> str_squish()
derived_rows <- str_count(read_file(here::here("original_extracted", "replication_archive", "code", "in_text_claims.R")), "expect = \"derived\"")

environment_line <- function(path, pattern) {
  read_lines(path) |> str_subset(pattern) |> first() |> str_squish()
}
info_deposit <- here::here("original_extracted", "replication_archive", "output", "session_info.txt")
info_rerun <- here::here("maintained", "archive_run", "replication_archive", "output", "session_info.txt")
csv_gap <- comparison |> filter(str_ends(file, "csv"), !is.na(measure)) |> pull(measure) |> max()
figure_slopes <- slopes |> filter(index != "rating_index", index != "intended" | dv %in% c("Favorability", "Vote Choice"))
```

*Drafted by Claude Opus 5.5 under the supervision of Alex Coppock.*

# Summary

This repository reruns the deposit of an article on whether the emotional content of campaign ads predicts their persuasive effects, compares the article and its appendix with the rerun, and lists the errors found.

- **The deposit runs.** All `r nrow(verdicts)` of its scripts finish without error, both in place and after every derived file is removed.
- **The page matches the deposit.** `r sum(gt$match_rewrite == 1, na.rm = TRUE)` of `r sum(!is.na(gt$match_rewrite))` extracted numbers agree at the printed precision, and so do all `r sum(floats$covered)` appendix table cells checked. The one disagreement is the two-ad sample size.
- **Matching the deposit does not make the numbers right.** Sanders favorability is rescaled twice in the deposit's cleaning script, which the article prints faithfully. See [Errata](#errata).
- **The article's central null holds under every correction computed here.** None of the `r nrow(figure_slopes)` refits of the Figure 2, 3, and 4 slopes reaches p < 0.05. These are the corrections listed in the errata and not all conceivable ones.
- **This repository holds no independent rewrite.** Every `value_rewrite` comes from rerunning the deposit's own code, so an error in that code that is not reported below would pass here too.

| Link | |
|---|---|
| Article | [10.1080/10584609.2026.2726266](https://doi.org/10.1080/10584609.2026.2726266) |
| Replication archive | [10.7910/DVN/CB3LP1](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/CB3LP1) |
| Errata | `murphy_etal_2026_errata.pdf` in this repository |

**Layout.** `original/` holds the deposit's zip once fetched and `original_extracted/` its contents; neither is redistributed. `maintained/` holds the rerun, the comparison, and the refits. `ground_truth/` holds the extraction from the published page and the comparison with the rerun. `errata.qmd` is the source of the errata note, and `errata_entries.csv` is its machine-readable copy.

**To reproduce.** Download the repository, open `murphy_etal_2026.Rproj`, and run `source("run_all.R")`. The stripped rerun and the accuracy rerun each took between 10 and 15 minutes here. Set the environment variable `MURPHY_REUSE_ARCHIVE_RUN=TRUE` to reuse a finished one.

# Paper overview

The article reports 29 waves of survey experiments fielded by YouGov during the 2016 presidential campaign, in which subjects saw a campaign ad or a placebo. It regresses each ad's conditional average treatment effect on favorability, vote choice, turnout, and issue support on subjects' average emotional reactions to that ad, and finds slopes that are close to zero.

# Original archive reproducibility

The deposit is `r nrow(manifest)` zip with `r nrow(members)` members, all of which match the manifest on MD5 and byte size. It ran in two passes.

| Pass | Starting point | Scripts OK | Scripts failed |
|---|---|---|---|
| In place | The deposit as shipped | `r sum(verdicts$in_place == "OK")` | `r sum(verdicts$in_place != "OK")` |
| Stripped | Every file in `output/`, `data/estimates/`, and both cleaned data files removed | `r sum(verdicts$stripped == "OK")` | `r sum(verdicts$stripped != "OK")` |

Each script's verdict in both passes is in `maintained/output/archive_script_verdicts.csv`. The in-place pass overwrote every derived file, which leaves six input files as the only ones older than the run. That pass was run once from an unzipped copy, and its log is `maintained/output/archive_inplace_run.log`. `run_all.R` repeats only the stripped pass.

The stripped rerun's `r nrow(comparison)` output files compare with the deposited ones as follows.

```{r comparison}
comparison |>
  count(verdict, name = "files") |>
  kable()
```

- The four CSVs that differ do so by at most `r sprintf("%.1e", csv_gap)`, which is numerical noise.
- Three PDFs differ beyond their timestamp and R version. Figures A.2 and E.7, and their PNGs, use `position_jitter` with no seed, so they differ from one run to the next. Figure 1's PDF differs in one text coordinate by 0.01 points, 65.35 against 65.36, read from its decompressed stream. The other PNGs differ in at most `r sprintf("%.2f", 100 * max(comparison$measure[str_ends(comparison$file, "png") & !str_detect(comparison$file, "a2_|e7_")]))` percent of channel values, from rasterization, and their PDFs agree.

The deposit's audit script ends with this line:

> `r claim_summary_line`

Read it with care. "Asserted" counts every row, including the `r derived_rows` that its source marks `expect = "derived"`, which are printed and never compared. Those rows and one evidence line make up "unasserted", which is why asserted exceeds matched with nothing mismatched. The two-ad sample size is one of those rows, so the summary cannot fail on it.

# Errata {#errata}

The note lists `r nrow(spine)` entries: `r sum(spine$form == "correction")` corrected quantities, `r sum(spine$form == "brief")` brief corrections to the text, and `r sum(spine$form == "note")` notes that correct nothing because neither the page nor the deposit settles what was intended.

```{r errata-table}
spine |>
  transmute(Entry = entry, Item = title, Form = form) |>
  kable()
```

## Read and not filed

These were read and left out of the errata. They are recorded so that a later reader need not rediscover them.

- **"Each week" (p. 4).** The deposit has 29 dated waves spanning 34 weeks, with six 14-day gaps. The sentence describes what happened in a week with a wave, and "29 weeks of experiments" counts those waves correctly, so no text is wrong.
- **`will_vote`.** `clean_exps.R` codes `match_DTHC` 1 and 2 as 1 and 9 as 0, and leaves code 8 missing, which is 748 raw responses. The deposit holds no codebook to name that code, and the article prints no statement about it, so there is nothing on the page to correct.
- **"CORRECTED AT PROOF" comments in `in_text_claims.R`.** They sit beside stale quotations of earlier wording. The values checked here agree with the published PDF, so this concerns the deposit's comments and not the article.

# Ground truth

`ground_truth/murphy_etal_2026_ground_truth.csv` holds `r nrow(gt)` claims: `r sum(gt$claim_type == "pipeline")` numbers compared with the rerun and `r sum(gt$claim_type == "descriptive")` descriptive statements given a computed verdict. `value_paper` is what the page prints, and `value_rewrite` is the rerun's value. Rows the errata reports carry a `defect_locus`. The descriptive verdicts are `r sum(gt$holds == 1, na.rm = TRUE)` holding and `r sum(gt$holds == 0, na.rm = TRUE)` not holding.

# The extraction and the two instruments

`published_claims.csv` covers the slopes printed in Figures 2, 3, and 4, the Figure E.10 slope, and the counts and reliabilities in the text. It leaves uncovered most of the matchup percentages and wave sizes that the deposit's own audit checks. `published_appendix_values.csv` and `published_table_d16.csv` cover the appendix's regression tables and its ad-coding table.

The two instruments are the comparison in `build_ground_truth.R` and the deposit's own `in_text_claims.R`, which is reported above. Neither can detect an error that the page and the code share, and the largest entries in the errata are of that kind. They came from reading the code and from a range table of the cleaned variables.

`build_ground_truth.R` halts on a broken join, a claim with no value or verdict, a spine id with no extraction row, a number that disagrees with the page and is absent from the spine, and any disagreeing appendix cell.

| Float | Published numbers | Agreeing |
|---|---|---|
| Regression tables | `r sum(floats$published_numbers[floats$table != "D.16"])` | `r sum(floats$covered[floats$table != "D.16"])` |
| Table D.16 | `r floats$published_numbers[floats$table == "D.16"]` | `r floats$covered[floats$table == "D.16"]` |

`ground_truth/negative_controls.R` breaks one input at a time and requires the matching gate to stop the build. All `r sum(controls$outcome == controls$expected)` of `r nrow(controls)` runs behave as required. These runs show that the gates fire on these faults and say nothing about faults not tried.

# Maintained rewrite

There is none. The deposit is recent code in the same style this project would write, so this repository reruns it and adds `maintained/corrected_slopes.R`, which refits the published meta-regressions on the deposit's own estimates under the corrections. That script's published specification returns every printed cell of Tables C.1, C.6, C.11, and E.17 before it applies a correction. `maintained/corrected_accuracy.R` reruns the deposit's two accuracy bootstraps with the duplicated Sanders line deleted and the deposit's seed, since those results are not linear in the CATEs. An independent rewrite remains undone, and it is what could catch a further error in the estimation code.

# Figure verification

Figures are compared through the rerun's files in the table above, and through the slope labels on Figures 2, 3, and 4 in the ground truth. Nobody compared the published figures with the rerun's by eye.
